comparison: Both evaluations agree on the structural identification of metal ions (Zn2+ and Ca2+) in the RCK domain. OpenEval R2 finds crystallographic and functional data support the inhibitory role of Ca2+, while peer R8 acknowledges the structural observations of metal coordination without criticism. High concordance on structural findings (C33-C38, C40-C41, C43).

Strong disagreement on nucleotide activation claims (C2-C3, C44, C57-C59). OpenEval finds converging evidence from flux assays and electrophysiology supporting nucleotide-specific activation. Peer reviewers question whether nucleotides substantially activate the channel, noting weak functional effects versus tight structural binding, and suggest calling them 'modulators' rather than 'ligands'.

Disagreement on K+ selectivity classification (C47-C49). OpenEval supports the permeability measurements and selectivity characterization. Peer reviewers challenge classifying GsuK as a K+ channel, noting that large inward currents would be carried by Na+ under the experimental conditions, making it 'a non-selective cation channel' rather than a K+ channel.

Both acknowledge the Ca2+ affinity discrepancy and closed-state structures (C106-C111). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative explanations for the discrepancy. Peer reviewers acknowledge the observation that only closed states were captured without challenging it, though they criticize mechanistic interpretations built from these structures.

Partial disagreement on nucleotide binding structures (C74-C80, C88-C89). OpenEval supports the crystallographic identification of ADP configurations. Peer reviewers accept structural observations but question functional interpretation, noting the disconnect between tight crystal binding and weak electrophysiological effects, suggesting uncertainty about whether the crystallographic site mediates activation.

Disagreement on Ca2+ inhibition mechanism (C4, C21, C50-C53, C85-C86). OpenEval strongly supports that Ca2+ acts through the RCK domain site affecting gating. Peer reviewers question whether this is the sole mechanism, noting that pore blockade hasn't been adequately excluded since only inward currents are shown, and other mechanisms cannot be ruled out.

Agreement on the segmented inner helix structural observation (C5). Both evaluations acknowledge this as a valid and novel structural finding. OpenEval supports it as directly observed crystallographically. Peer reviewers explicitly note this produces 'a second bundle crossing' and acknowledge it without criticism.

Strong disagreement on GsuK-BK/Slo similarities (C114-C121, C90, C118-C121). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting claims require validation. Peer reviewers explicitly reject the comparison, stating 'it seems more reasonable to claim that GsuK and Slo1 have different gating mechanisms' and citing literature showing BK channels lack significant cytoplasmic gates.

Agreement that gating mechanism claims are speculative (C93-C94, C101-C105 overlap with C6, C96-C104). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to lack of open-state structure. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, calling this 'The major weakness' involving 'extreme interpretation' and stating 'assertions of details about the gating mechanisms are not supported by the data, beyond suggesting interesting hypotheses'.

Partial overlap on NAD+ binding (C81-C84). OpenEval supports the crystallographic identification of NAD+ and its distinct binding mode. Peer R9 addresses broader nucleotide binding concerns, questioning whether crystallographic sites mediate functional activation, which indirectly affects confidence in NAD+ functional claims.

Disagreement on opening mechanism inferences (C70-C72, C95-C100 overlap with C6, C96-C98, C100). OpenEval supports structural differences and finds opening mechanism inference reasonable despite both structures being closed. Peer reviewers reject mechanistic interpretations as overreaching given only closed states are available.

Agreement on structural observations of gating ring rotation and linker configuration (C63-C64). Both evaluations acknowledge the structural finding that the gating ring is rotated relative to transmembrane domains compared to MthK. No concerns raised about the structural observation itself.

Agreement on segmented helix structural features (C65-C66). Both evaluations support the structural observations of the segmented inner helix. Peer R3 acknowledges the bend at a second site producing a second bundle crossing as a novel observation without criticism.

Agreement on L97D mutant functional effects (C54-C55). Both evaluations acknowledge that the L97D mutant shows altered/reduced calcium sensitivity. OpenEval supports systematic electrophysiology data. Peer reviewers acknowledge the functional observation without questioning the basic data.

Agreement on structural observations of L97D conformational differences (C95, C99). Both acknowledge structural differences between wild-type and L97D mutant. Peer R12 explicitly states only closed states were captured. Both accept the structural observations while differing on mechanistic interpretations.

Agreement on quality of structural determinations (C60). Both evaluations acknowledge the validity of the crystal structures obtained. Peer R7 states structures were obtained for multiple forms including gating ring and full-length channel without raising concerns about structural quality.

Minimal overlap on conserved binding sites (C90). OpenEval supports evolutionary conservation across channels. Peer R6 addresses broader BK comparison claims and rejects similarities in gating mechanisms, which contextually challenges the functional relevance of conserved sites.

OpenEval R1 addresses gating ring structural features (C19-C31) with crystallographic validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this comprehensive set of structural claims about the bi-lobed architecture, asymmetry, and closed gate configuration.

OpenEval R15 addresses speculative proposals about charged residues and lipid interactions (C69, C112-C113). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific hypotheses about functional roles of charged residues in lipid interaction and gating.
